$comment: Reference envelope for the prompt 'add a rate limiter to the HTTP middleware and run the tests'. Hand-written to illustrate the intended precision of a generated envelope: narrow path globs, a specific executable allowlist, a proxy-only network grant, and explicit denials carving dangerous paths out of a broad workspace write grant. Used as a schema fixture and as a few-shot example for the LLM analyzer.

intent.raw_prompt: add a rate limiter to the HTTP middleware and run the tests
intent.summary: Implement rate limiting in the HTTP middleware layer, then run the Go test suite to verify.
ambiguities: Rate limiting algorithm unspecified (token bucket vs sliding window).
Unclear whether an external rate-limiting dependency may be added, which would require network access to the module proxy.

grants.rationale: Read project sources to locate the middleware layer, plus the Go toolchain and module cache required to build.
The rate limiter and its tests belong in the middleware package. Writes are scoped to that package rather than the whole repo, so an edit elsewhere is a visible deviation.
New source files in the target package; the Go build cache writes to a temporary directory.

Building and testing requires the Go toolchain. The shell is included because the toolchain invokes it for cgo and generate steps. Note that arg_patterns is advisory only and is not a security boundary.
Only required if the implementation adds a dependency. Marked optional because a standard-library implementation needs no egress at all.
Name resolution for the module proxy, needed only if the optional network grant is exercised.

denials.rationale: Direct manipulation of git internals is never appropriate for a code-editing task and would let an agent rewrite history rather than make a reviewable change.
CI configuration is a privileged execution path. Modifying it converts a code change into an execution-environment change, which this task does not require.
Credential material is not required to implement a rate limiter. Reading it is the first half of the credential-access-then-egress pattern this system exists to catch.

modifications: Narrowed fs.write from /home/dev/project/** to the middleware package.
